articles.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
articles.summary: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server. Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 and rated

articles.title: PHP Fixes 7 Critical Flaws, Including Bugs That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
articles.summary: The PHP Foundation has released security updates to address multiple critical security flaws that could be exploited to achieve remote code execution on affected deployments, including CVE-2026-115560. articles.title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
articles.summary: A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an advisory published today. Fixed versions are out for all supported branches, and the company lists no workaround. vCenter is the central console for managing an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines. The

articles.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
articles.summary: Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site. That can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the project rates the vulnerable configurations as uncommon. Fixed releases for all supported branches shipped yesterday. articles.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
articles.summary: One of the early targets of PHP2Shell exploitation was the firewall. On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web server without authentication. The disclosure itself went a little wrong.

articles.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
articles.summary: N-able on Wednesday disclosed that unknown threat actors gained unauthorized access to one of the servers in the Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, causing it to disable management interfaces and APIs. articles.title: Ruby Releases Fixes for 7 Regex and String Flaws, Warns 5 Have Proof-of-Concept RCE
articles.summary: Ruby contains seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression engine and its string case-conversion code. For five of them, its maintainers say, proof-of-concept exploits, or PoCs, have shown that crafted input can run code on the machine. articles.summary: Low-privilege database accounts that cannot read a single application table can still be used to run code on the database server itself, a researcher has shown, by reaching memory-corruption bugs in the engine code behind ordinary SQL. articles.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
articles.summary: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely, a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom, was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources

articles.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
articles.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

articles.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
articles.summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

articles.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
articles.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices

articles.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
articles.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
articles.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

articles.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.
